subtopics.title: How the Theory Question Papers Are Built

questions.question: Each sixty-mark theory question in the Geography papers opens with:
options: Fifteen marks of short, objective-type questions

questions.question: The eight-mark paragraph question is marked as:
options: Eight facts at one mark each, bullets allowed
Two ideas at four marks each
Four ideas at two marks each, in full sentences only

questions.question: The cognitive-level split of the papers is:
options: A quarter lower order, half middle order, a quarter higher order
Half lower order, half higher order

subtopics.title: The Objective Opener — Fifteen Marks Before You Blink

questions.question: The eye of a tropical cyclone is a zone of:
options: Descending dry air, which is why it is calm and clear

questions.question: A misfit stream is evidence of:
Because there is no negative marking in the objective items, the best strategy is to:
options: Answer every item, using elimination when unsure
Copy the pattern of previous answers

subtopics.title: Walking a Climate Question — Synoptic Chart in Hand

questions.question: Two pieces of chart evidence that the season is winter are:
options: High-pressure cells lying north of their summer positions and a frontal system reaching the Cape
A tropical cyclone in the Mozambique Channel and heat over the plateau
Widely spaced isobars and no fronts anywhere
A coastal low and a berg wind

questions.question: For a two-mark identification question, the right answer length is:
options: One precise line, then move on

questions.question: The cold front misses Gauteng's rainfall mainly because:
options: The front's northern edge misses the plateau and the Kalahari High's stable descending air blocks uplift
The urban heat island repels fronts

subtopics.title: Walking a Geomorphology Question — River Capture on the Landscape

questions.question: River capture is defined as:
options: The natural diversion of one river's headwaters into a more vigorous neighbouring river through headward erosion
The damming of a river by engineers
The joining of two rivers at a confluence

questions.question: The dry notch left in the ridge after capture, the sharp bend, and the shrunken lower course are respectively:
options: Wind gap, elbow of capture, misfit stream

questions.question: River A captured river B because river A:
options: Had a steeper gradient, more erosive energy, and eroded headward through the watershed

subtopics.title: Walking a Settlement Question — The Emptying Platteland

questions.question: Rural depopulation is:
options: The long-term decline of a rural area's population as people move away, mainly to urban areas
The seasonal movement of farm workers

questions.question: From the Karoo extract, which pair are PUSH factors?
options: The tourism route and the processing plant
Mechanisation shedding farm labour and shrinking services like the closed bank
Cape Town's universities and Gauteng's wages

questions.question: In the eight-mark paragraph, each of the four ideas earns its second mark by:
options: Being developed with an explanation or because-clause in a full sentence

subtopics.title: Walking an Economic Geography Question — Corridors and Sectors

questions.question: A Spatial Development Initiative is:
options: A government strategy concentrating coordinated investment along a corridor with economic potential

questions.question: The Maputo Corridor benefits Gauteng's industries because it:
options: Gives the landlocked industrial core its shortest route to a deep-water port, cutting export costs

questions.question: Gauteng leads South African industry partly because it:
options: Has no competition from other regions
Grew on the goldfields, holds the largest market and skilled workforce, and centres the transport network

subtopics.title: The Eight-Mark Paragraph — Where Insight Becomes Marks

questions.question: The first move of the paragraph recipe is to:
options: Read and obey the instruction verb — discuss, evaluate or suggest

questions.question: A paragraph answer written as bullet points:
options: Breaks the paragraph contract — full sentences are compulsory

questions.question: In the model paragraph on informal settlements, 'upgrade in situ' is a strong idea because it:
options: Provides services while keeping communities intact, and the sentence develops that reason
